summary: Serving node heartbeat jitter and intermittent gRPC pipelining stalls caused by egress LB TCP connection aging
description: Issue summary: Customer reported intermittent increases in tail latency and occasional gRPC streaming stalls for large-model generation on their Dedicated deployment. Impact: Multiple production jobs experienced stalled token streaming and occasional kv-cache invalidation leading to higher token costs and retries. Environment: Dedicated cluster in prod us-east-1 behind customer's egress load balancer appliance + corporate SD-WAN. Steps to reproduce: 1) Start a streaming chat generation targeting neptune/gptx-13B with long context (>8k). 2) Observe occasional near-instant latency spikes (~500-2000ms) for 1-3s windows and then return to baseline. 3) On some runs, the gRPC stream shows repeated KEEPALIVE/FIN/RESET sequence, followed by a partial model-shard range re-request. Observed behavior: Periodic gRPC pipelining stalls coincident with TCP connection close/reuse events from the customer egress LB. Expected behavior: Stable streaming with continuous kv-cache reuse and no shard re-requests. Logs and traces: Customer attached tcpdump snippets showing FIN followed by new SYN on same 5-tuple within ~1.2s, conntrack logs showing TCP CLOSE_WAIT spikes, and serving node logs showing "kv-cache-flush: peer-conn-reset". Support runbook references: heartbeat-flap-runbook and streaming-gateway-timeouts.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: egress LB (third-party NVA) has aggressive TCP idle-termination/aging behavior that causes mid-stream connection reset. When the serving runtime receives a FIN and a rapid SYN reestablishing a different TCP socket, gRPC multiplexing semantics lead to in-flight streams being half-closed and the runtime dropping KV cache references for those sessions. Evidence: - Customer tcpdump (attached) shows NVA issuing active TCP FIN on long-lived keepalive connections after ~10s of idleness; their NVA documentation has an "aggressive idle reclaim" mode. - Server-side system logs show increased SO_LINGER/TCP_ABORT messages and repeated range re-requests from model shard fetcher. - Control-plane heartbeats show small but visible jitter coincident with the TCP events. - Reproduced in staging by replicating NVA idle-close behavior using HAProxy/TCP reset script: same gRPC pipelining stalls and KV-cache eviction observed. Correlation matrix: tail-latency spikes line up with the customer's egress LB idle timeout, not with model size or request rate. Additional details: - conntrack metrics indicate ephemeral port reuse on the client egress path within 1-3s causing server to observe new SYNs with overlapping 4-tuple. - The runtime's current strategy treats connection resets as stronger signal to evict per-connection caches; this results in extra downstream artifact re-requests.
comments: 2026-03-13 09:22 - Ava Martinez (Support): Customer opened ticket after seeing repeated stalls. Provided tcpdump and NVA config export. Asked customer to confirm whether appliance had 'TCP idle reclaim' enabled.

2026-03-13 11:05 - Neptune SRE (customer): Confirmed they were running vendor firmware with 'idle-reclaim=10s' enabled for aggressive connection churn. They cannot upgrade immediately due to change window.

2026-03-13 13:40 - Ravi Desai (SRE): Reproduced locally by simulating idle-close at 10s. Observed identical gRPC half-close pattern and kv-cache eviction. Opening engineering follow-up: GH PR referenced above.

2026-03-13 15:10 - Support (Ava): Suggested two immediate mitigations for customer: 1) Increase NVA idle timeout to >= 90s or 2) enable target-side SO_KEEPALIVE and increase keepalive probes interval to keep connection active. Customer applied soft-change to 45s as partial mitigation.

2026-03-14 08:30 - Neptune SRE: After increasing idle timeout to 45s, tail-latency spikes dropped ~92% and stalls stopped in observed window. They temporarily scheduled a vendor firmware upgrade to disable aggressive reclaim.

2026-03-14 12:00 - Ravi Desai (SRE): Applied internal workaround guidance to runtime: relax per-connection cache eviction on abrupt resets (canary flag enabled in prod-serving group). Sent PR to add metrics for tcp-close-rate and kv-cache-evictions to runtime telemetry.
2026-03-14 16:05 - Support (Ava): Marking ticket resolved after customer confirmed stable behavior in 24h smoke tests. Follow-up actions documented.
resolution: Workaround and fix: 1) Customer mitigation — increased egress NVA idle timeout from 10s to 45s; planned firmware upgrade to remove aggressive reclaim setting. 2) Temporary platform mitigation — enabled canary flag to relax immediate KV cache eviction on abrupt connection resets for a subset of serving nodes. 3) Long-term engineering action — runtime PR to better detect true connection quiescence vs aggressive L4 idle reclaim and add metrics (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4592). Rollout notes: Canary change enabled 2026-03-14 on 10% of serving pods in us-east-1, monitored for 48h. Customer verification: Neptune SRE ran targeted load and reported elimination of stalls; no regression in throughput observed. Follow-ups: - Add alert for TCP-close-rate > 0.5% on serving nodes. - Document recommended NVA idle timeout (>=90s) and SO_KEEPALIVE tuning in Private Deploy networking checklist.
